subject: physics
title: Ultrasound, infrasound and seismic waves
key_idea: Ultrasound is above 20 kHz and infrasound below 20 Hz. Echoes from ultrasound give the distance to a boundary, using the time for the echo and half the distance travelled. Seismic P-waves and S-waves show the structure of the Earth.

blocks.text: (Separate science) Ultrasound is sound with a frequency too high for humans to hear. It is used to find the distance to a hidden boundary by timing its echo.

items.meaning: Sound with a frequency above 20 000 Hz (20 kHz).
Sound with a frequency below 20 Hz.
A reflected wave returning to its source.

items: Ultrasound is partially reflected whenever it meets a boundary between two different materials.
A detector measures the time for the reflection to arrive back.
Some of the pulse carries on through the boundary, so there can be more than one echo.

blocks.label: Distance from an echo
where: distance to the boundary, in metres (m)
speed of the wave in the material, in metres per second (m/s)
time between sending the pulse and receiving the echo, in seconds (s)

blocks.text: The pulse travels to the boundary and back, so halve the time, or halve the distance, before the last step.

items.text: An echo returns after 0.040 s. The pulse travelled there and back.
Sound travels at 1500 m/s in sea water. Depth = 1500 × 0.020 = 30 m.

items: Ultrasound has a frequency above 20 kHz. Infrasound is below 20 Hz.
An echo is a reflection at a boundary between two materials.
Use half the echo time (or double distance) to find the distance to the boundary.

blocks.text: Different materials reflect ultrasound at their boundaries. This lets us look at things we cannot see directly.

rows: Medical imaging, such as a foetal scan
Pulses reflect from boundaries between layers of tissue. Each layer returns an echo at a different time. A computer uses the times to build an image.
A ship sends pulses to the sea bed. The time for the echo gives the depth. Objects in deep water also reflect pulses.
Echoes show the position of boundaries inside a solid that cannot be seen from outside.

items: Three layers of tissue give three echoes from each pulse.
The longer the time between echoes, the thicker the layer.
The speed of ultrasound in the tissue must be known, so the depth can be calculated from speed × time.
Ultrasound reflects from boundaries between tissues, so it can be used for imaging.
The time for each echo gives the depth of that boundary.
Sonar works in the same way to find the depth of water or detect objects.

blocks.text: Earthquakes produce seismic waves. They travel through the Earth and give evidence about parts of the Earth we cannot see.

items: A seismometer detects the waves from an earthquake.
The P-wave arrives first, then the S-wave. The time between them is directly proportional to the distance from the earthquake.
S-waves do not travel through the outer core.
So the outer core must be a liquid.
The region where S-waves are not detected shows the size of the liquid outer core.
Waves change speed and direction at boundaries between layers, which shows that the Earth has layers.
The speeds of P-waves and S-waves generally increase with depth, as the material gets denser.
P-waves are longitudinal. S-waves are transverse and cannot travel through a liquid.
S-waves do not reach the other side of the Earth, so the outer core is liquid.
Seismic waves gave new evidence about parts of the Earth that cannot be seen.

checks.q: Describe the difference between infrasound and ultrasound.
checks.a: Infrasound has a frequency below 20 Hz. Ultrasound has a frequency above 20 000 Hz.

checks.q: An ultrasound pulse takes 0.60 s to go to the sea bed and back. The speed of ultrasound in sea water is 1500 m/s. Calculate the depth of the sea.
checks.a: Time to the sea bed = 0.60 ÷ 2 = 0.30 s. Depth = 1500 × 0.30 = 450 m.

checks.q: Explain why seismic waves are evidence that the Earth's outer core is a liquid.
checks.a: S-waves cannot travel through a liquid. S-waves do not travel through the outer core, so the outer core must be a liquid.

exam_phrases: S-waves cannot travel through a liquid
S-waves do not travel through the (outer) core
the distance is (directly) proportional to the time between the two waves arriving

mistakes.wrong: Some seismic waves do not go through the core, so the core is liquid.
mistakes.right: This gets 1 of 2 marks. Name the waves: S-waves cannot travel through a liquid, and S-waves do not travel through the outer core.

mistakes.wrong: The greater the distance, the greater the time between the P-wave and S-wave.
mistakes.right: This gets 1 of 2 marks. Say that the distance is directly proportional to the time between the two waves arriving.

worked_example.question:
P-waves and S-waves are two types of seismic wave caused by earthquakes.

Explain why the study of seismic waves provides evidence for the structure of the Earth's core.
answer_points: S-waves cannot travel through a liquid.
S-waves do not travel through the (outer) core.
worked_example.tip: Each point is one mark. Say S-waves, not just seismic waves.

exam_phrases: pulses reflected by / bounce off / echo off ocean bed
time between emission and receipt of pulse measured
velocity of sound in sea water known
either distance halved or time halved

mistakes.right: The pulse goes to the sea floor and back, so the half was missed. D = ½ × 1500 × 0.048 = 36 m. Ignoring the half scores 1 mark.

mistakes.wrong: Infrasound has a lower frequency than ultrasound.
mistakes.right: This gets 1 of 2 marks. Give the values too: infrasound is below 20 Hz and ultrasound is above 20 000 Hz.

mistakes.wrong: Sound is sent to the ocean bed and back, the time is measured and distance = speed × time.
mistakes.right: Level 3 needs two of: ultrasound, pulses, and halving the distance or the time. Halve the time (or the distance), or the depth comes out twice too big.

blocks.text: Uses of ultrasound and infrasound include sonar, foetal scanning and the exploration of the Earth's core. The seismic wave evidence is in the section above.

worked_example.question:
A transducer on the bottom of a ship can transmit and detect ultrasonic waves.

The waves reflect off the sea floor and are received back at the transducer.

The waves travel at 1500 m/s.

The time between transmission and reception is 48 milliseconds.

Calculate the depth of the water, D.
worked_example.tip: Change 48 ms to 0.048 s first. The answer 72 m, from ignoring the half, scores 1 mark.

exam_phrases: Depth can be calculated by speed × time
takes different times to travel (there and back) through different layers
the thicker the layer, the bigger the time interval
S waves do not travel through the core
so the outer core is a liquid
speed (of P/S waves) increases as density increases

mistakes.right: The time is for there and back. Divide by 2: 1500 × (2.8 × 10⁻⁷ ÷ 2) = 2.1 × 10⁻⁴ m. Not dividing by 2 loses a mark.

mistakes.wrong: S waves do not travel through the core.
mistakes.right: Finish the argument: S waves do not travel through the core, so the outer core is a liquid.

worked_example.question:
Ultrasound waves are used to produce images of the inside of the human body.

The ultrasound waves reflect from the boundary between two different materials inside the human body.

A computer records a time of 2.8 × 10⁻⁷ s between emitting one ultrasound wave and receiving the reflection of this wave from the boundary between the fat tissue and the muscle tissue.

The speed of ultrasound waves in fat tissue is 1500 m/s.

Calculate the thickness of the fat tissue.
answer_points: Select the equation: distance = speed × time.
worked_example.tip: The time is divided by 2 because the wave travels to the boundary and back.
